# Part I: The Moonshot and Its Motivation {.unnumbered}

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
Part I defines the Architecture 2.0 moonshot and establishes why rising hardware-software complexity requires AI-assisted design space exploration without surrendering human commitment authority.
:::

## Part Objectives

- Translate compact system intent into explicit, multi-layer hardware-software architecture specifications.
- Delineate candidate generation velocity from downstream physical verification capacity to diagnose design loop bottlenecks.
- Establish the Total-Cost Boundary to evaluate full system trade-offs across compute, memory bandwidth, power, and verification cost.

## Part Map

- **@sec-moonshot (The Architecture 2.0 Moonshot):** Introduces the moonshot vision, the 8-layer Lighthouse Prompt Stack, and the principle of 100% In-Order Commit Authority.
- **@sec-design-loop-no-longer-scales (Why Architecture Work Is Getting Harder):** Analyzes the compounding pressures of Dennard scaling collapse, search space explosion, and evaluation capacity bounds.

## Guiding Questions

1. How can compact system intent become an executable architecture specification without diluting system obligations or human decision ownership?
2. Why does candidate generation velocity outpace downstream verification capacity, creating critical evaluation bottlenecks across the design loop?
